text:
Erin: Heads-up — after today's NF4/FP4 canary push I'm seeing a sustained tail-latency increase and memory climb on hybrid hosts. KV hit ratio also dropped. cc @Mateo @Priya :eyes:

perf-bot: ALERT: quant4-canary: throughput -12% vs baseline, p99 +15%, KV hit ratio -18% — link: https://perf/reports/2165439999

Mateo: can you paste a short perf profile and the kernel-selection log? especially kernel_select timings.

Erin: putting quick flame/prof snippet from canary host (top 200ms)
```text
kernel_select 45.2%
batch_coordinator_wait 20.1%
kv_lookup 18.3%
host_memcpy 9.8%
quant_dequant_fallback 6.6%
```

Priya: interesting — 'quant_dequant_fallback' shows up. calibration might be producing out-of-range activations forcing slowpath. Did we see any kernel fallback entries? That would explain memcpy/host path.

Jin: kernel-selector log (short):
```text
[12:03:01] model=llm-nf4 v=3.2 selector: prefer=quant4 nf4 kernel
[12:03:01] selector: detected activation_scale > threshold -> fallback to fp4_host_kernel
[12:03:01] selector: batch=small (<=8) -> microbatching enabled
```

Alex: microbatching + fallback = lots of tiny host memcpy's, KV cache thrash. Try bumping microbatch window from 8->32 for canary and disable hybrid-slab allocator to see if slab fragmentation is the culprit.

Erin: agreed. Mateo @Mateo can you run canary with flags: `--microbatch-window=32 --alloc=slab:none` and the patch `disable-hybrid-slab`? I'll keep an eye.

Mateo: running now. ETA ~8m.

deploy-bot: Started canary deploy 2165440007 with flags `microbatch=32 alloc=slab:none` by Mateo

Mateo: quick result after 10m: p99 down ~8%, throughput back to -3% vs baseline, memory climb stopped. KV hit ratio recovered ~+12%.

Erin: :thumbsup: nice. Two immediate follow-ups:
- add telemetry for 'kernel_fallback_reason' to catch calibration-induced fallbacks
- add gating in calibration to prefer degraded quant params over fallback unless severe quality loss
- long-term: investigate hybrid-slab fragmentation pattern under quantized KV layout

Priya: I'll own the calibration gating RFC.

Jin: I'll add selector telemetry and a small unit test for activation_scale threshold behavior.

Alex: I'll schedule an overnight job to run a stress matrix across batch sizes and activation distributions.

Erin: thanks team. leaving this thread open til RFC + telemetry merged. :white_check_mark:
